title: About Me
text:
About Me
Eugene Sogbe is a researcher in transport and mobility who has completed his PhD in Transport Engineering at Monash University Malaysia. He holds a Bachelor of Technology (B.Tech) in Automotive Engineering with First-Class Honours from Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Ghana, and a Higher National Diploma (HND) in Mechanical Engineering, with a major in Automotive Engineering, from Ho Technical University, Ghana. His academic experience includes teaching and supporting undergraduate education at both Ho Technical University and Monash University Malaysia. At Ho Technical University, he progressed from Teaching Assistant to Coursework Instructor, gaining experience in undergraduate teaching, course delivery, assessment, and student academic support. At Monash University Malaysia, he has served as a Teaching Assistant in the Department of Civil Engineering, supporting undergraduate workshops and practical classes alongside his doctoral research.
Before joining Monash University Malaysia, Eugene gained more than four years of professional engineering experience as a Supervising Engineer at DESK-Air Engineering Consult. In this role, he was involved in the management and delivery of engineering projects, overseeing day-to-day operations, resources, project staff, and contractors. His responsibilities included contract administration, budgeting, procurement and purchasing, financial transactions, and ensuring the delivery of quality engineering services. This professional experience complements his academic background by providing practical experience in project management, engineering operations, and the application of technical knowledge in professional settings.
Eugene’s research employs a combination of quantitative and qualitative approaches to investigate transport and mobility problems. His methodological experience includes Structural Equation Modelling (SEM), Latent Class Analysis (LCA), survey-based behavioural research, statistical analysis, and qualitative analysis, including thematic analysis. His research is also theoretically informed by established frameworks drawn from environmental psychology, behavioural science, and information systems and technology adoption. These include the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) model, Person–Environment Fit Theory, the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2), the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB), and Environmental Stress Theory. He uses these approaches and frameworks to examine behavioural responses, technology adoption, perceptions, attitudes, and decision-making within transport and mobility contexts.
Eugene contributes to the academic community through peer-review and professional service activities. He has reviewed manuscripts for a range of international journals in transport, mobility, safety, and urban studies, including Accident Analysis and Prevention, Public Transport, Travel Behaviour and Society, Journal of Transport Geography, Transport Policy, Transportation Research Interdisciplinary Perspectives, Transportation, Transportation Research Part D: Transport and Environment, Research in Transportation Business & Management and Cities. He has also contributed to academic and professional activities through conference and seminar organisation and other early-career researcher initiatives. Through these activities, he seeks to contribute not only through his own research but also to the broader development of the transport and mobility research community.

title: Eugene Sogbe, PhD

Researcher in Transport and Mobility
I am a researcher in transport and mobility specialising in public transport, travel behaviour, transport safety, and transport planning. My research seeks to improve transport systems through a deeper understanding of travel behaviour, evidence-based planning, and the development of safer, more sustainable mobility solutions.

title: Eugene Sogbe, PhD
text:
Research Areas


🚉 Public Transport
Understanding and improving public transport systems, service quality, accessibility, and ridership.


🚶 Travel Behaviour
Investigating behavioural factors influencing travel choices and mobility patterns.


🛡️ Transport Safety
Improving transport safety through behavioural research and evidence-based interventions.


🗺 Transport Planning
Supporting sustainable and efficient transport systems through planning and policy research.

title: Eugene Sogbe
text:
This doctoral research examined the factors shaping public transport use, ridership, passenger experiences, accessibility, and travel behaviour. The research brought together behavioural and transport-planning perspectives to develop a deeper understanding of public transport use across different user groups and contexts.



This doctoral research investigated the adoption of Mobility-as-a-Service (MaaS) and the factors shaping individuals’ intentions and preferences toward integrated mobility services. The research examined differences among potential user groups and explored the behavioural factors associated with MaaS adoption.






An ongoing study examining the adoption of bike-sharing as a sustainable mobility option in university settings. The research explores factors influencing perceptions and intentions toward bike-sharing and contributes to understanding sustainable campus mobility.



An ongoing study investigating how experiences and perceptions of the urban travel environment influence travel behaviour and decisions about continuing, avoiding, or changing modes of travel.



An ongoing study examining how passengers respond to unexpected public transport service disruptions, with a focus on passenger decision-making, behavioural responses, and coping strategies.
